abstract: Dynamic remodelling of multiprotein signalling complexes allows cells to rapidly adapt signalling strength. At synapses, neurotransmitter receptors and scaffolds concentrate in subsynaptic nanoclusters that govern synaptic signalling strength and that are dynamically remodelled by synaptic activity. However, although this distinct nanoscale organization of synaptic protein complexes is well-established, the mechanisms that control the activity-induced reorganization of these complexes remain elusive. Here, to resolve the mechanisms underlying the activity-induced spatiotemporal reorganization of the PSD, we combined CRISPR/Cas9-mediated tagging of endogenous synaptic proteins and quantitative super-resolution microscopy. We found that synaptic potentiation drives a rapid and long-lasting increase in the number and density of PSD scaffold nanoclusters. Strikingly, activity-induced reorganization of scaffold proteins originated in deep PSD layers and preceded AMPA receptor repositioning, indicating that newly recruited receptors populate preformed scaffold nanoclusters. Computational simulations support that this reorganization is sufficient to drive potentiation of synaptic responses. Mechanistically, we found that the interaction between the scaffold SHANK3 and the actin cytoskeleton is essential for activity-induced PSD nanocluster remodelling. Altogether, our findings present a novel mechanism through which cytoskeletal interactions remodel the spatial organization of the PSD, advancing our understanding of how the dynamic nanoscale reorganization of protein complexes can drive neuronal signalling.
